tasks.title: DecisionEngine routing: slider scoped to lossy classes + PNG/alpha branch (AC-C1, AC-C2 routing)
tasks.description: Rework DecisionEngine's classification-to-codec switch so the quality slider affects only Photo/Screenshot/LineArt, Monochrome and ScannedText ignore it, and the PNG codec is selected for alpha images and for Screenshot/LineArt under MaxQuality with no slider. Extend CompressionParams (and the compress call, via defaults/overload) with hasAlpha/bitsPerComponent/colorSpace so PDFOptimizer can drive the lossless branch without breaking existing callers.
acceptance_criteria: Given one image of each classification (Photo, Screenshot, LineArt, ScannedText, Monochrome), when DecisionEngine::compress is called with qualityHint=70 and again with qualityHint=0 under the same profile, then the output StreamFilter is unchanged between the two calls for ScannedText (JPXDecode) and Monochrome (FlateDecode), while Photo, Screenshot and LineArt select the lossy DCTDecode path when the slider is active (qualityHint=70).

Given hasAlpha=true (an image carrying /SMask or /Mask), when DecisionEngine::compress runs, then the PNG codec (m_pngCodec) is selected and the reported StreamFilter is FlateDecode, so JPEG-with-alpha flattening no longer occurs on this path.

Given Screenshot or LineArt under MaxQuality with no slider (qualityHint<=0), when DecisionEngine::compress runs, then the lossless PNG path (m_pngCodec, StreamFilter FlateDecode) is selected instead of JPEG, and existing Photo/Monochrome/ScannedText behavior is preserved (existing DecisionEngine tests still pass).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given one image of each classification (Photo, Screenshot, LineArt, ScannedText, Monochrome), when DecisionEngine::compress is called with qualityHint=70 and again with qualityHint=0 under the same profile, then the output StreamFilter is unchanged between the two calls for ScannedText (JPXDecode) and Monochrome (FlateDecode), while Photo, Screenshot and LineArt select the lossy DCTDecode path when the slider is active (qualityHint=70).
tests.description: TEST(DecisionEngine, SliderOnlyAffectsLossyClasses): for each classification, call compress twice (qualityHint 70 vs 0) and assert ScannedText==JPXDecode both, Monochrome==FlateDecode both, and Photo/Screenshot/LineArt==DCTDecode with the slider active.
tests.expected_result: TEST(DecisionEngine, SliderOnlyAffectsLossyClasses) passes; slider never changes the filter for ScannedText/Monochrome.

tests.expected_result: Alpha selects the PNG/FlateDecode path; m_pngCodec is reachable by a TEST(DecisionEngine, ...).

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given Screenshot or LineArt under MaxQuality with no slider (qualityHint<=0), when DecisionEngine::compress runs, then the lossless PNG path (m_pngCodec, StreamFilter FlateDecode) is selected instead of JPEG, and existing Photo/Monochrome/ScannedText behavior is preserved (existing DecisionEngine tests still pass).

tasks.title: Activate stream dedup via ReferenceRewriter referrer-repoint + distinct-duplicate fixture + P1-T3 rewrite (AC-C5)
tasks.description: Replace the inert ESC-001 isIndirect guard and the infeasible replaceObject call in PDFOptimizer's dedup loop with reference-rewriting: for each duplicate stream A byte-identical to kept B (FNV hash + dict-key signature, additionally requiring /Filter and /DecodeParms to match), a cycle-safe referrer walk over getAllObjects() + trailer repoints every reference to A -> B via QPDFObjectHandle::replaceKey / setArrayItem; A then drops under the already-set setPreserveUnreferencedObjects(false). Introduce a focused ReferenceRewriter component (src/core/ReferenceRewriter.{h,cpp}), add a staged $TMPDIR fixture distinct_duplicate_streams.pdf that actually references both distinct byte-identical streams, and rewrite the Phase-1 P1-T3 test to assert streamsDeduplicated>=1 with defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Given a staged $TMPDIR fixture distinct_duplicate_streams.pdf with two distinct indirect stream objects sharing byte-identical raw data and matching signatures (same /Subtype /Width /Height /ColorSpace /BitsPerComponent, plus matching /Filter and /DecodeParms), where BOTH streams are actually referenced from page content/resources (e.g. /Resources /XObject << /Im1 A /Im2 B >> with both drawn on the page) - not the reference-shared transparency.pdf and not added to the canonical 14 - when optimized with defaults (deduplicateStreams=true), then result.streamsDeduplicated>=1 and the output shares one stream object for that pair (every reference to A is repointed to B; QPDF().processFile clean; qpdf --json shows a single stream).
Given the same fixture, when optimized with --no-dedup (deduplicateStreams=false), then result.streamsDeduplicated==0 and both distinct stream objects remain.

Given the Phase-1 P1-T3 test in tests/test_structure_writer.cpp, when it is rewritten for this phase, then it asserts streamsDeduplicated>=1 with defaults against the new fixture and ==0 for the --no-dedup run, while the shared-XObject checks remain valid and all outputs pass QPDF().processFile.

context.architecture_excerpt:
| Stream dedup replace path | [new/changed] | Replaces the inert ESC-001 isIndirect() skip and the replaceObject call with a reference-rewriting path: for each duplicate stream A byte-identical to kept B, repoint every reference to A to B, then let A drop under the already-set setPreserveUnreferencedObjects(false). Retains the byte-identical signature detection (FNV hash + five dict keys), the objGen != guard and per-pair try/catch; streamsDeduplicated now increments for distinct byte-identical indirect streams (AC-C5, Phase 2). replaceObject is no longer called - it cannot alias duplicate streams. |
| ReferenceRewriter (core/ReferenceRewriter.{h,cpp}) | [new] | Cycle-safe referrer walk over every object (pdf.getAllObjects() + trailer) and its direct nested dicts/arrays; for a target objGen it repoints matching indirect references via replaceKey / setArrayItem. Never follows indirect references during traversal (each object is visited once from getAllObjects()), so cycles terminate and cost is bounded by object count. Only invoked when the byte-identical signature + objGen != guard already matched, and only for /Filter/DecodeParms-compatible streams (AC-C5, Phase 2) |
context.plan_excerpt:
- Product fix (reference-rewriting): in src/core/PDFOptimizer.cpp replace the inert ESC-001 indirect-handle skip and the replaceObject call with a reference-rewriting path - a new ReferenceRewriter helper walks every object (pdf.getAllObjects() + trailer) and its direct nested dicts/arrays, finds every indirect reference to the duplicate's objGen, and repoints it to the kept object via replaceKey / setArrayItem; the now-unreferenced duplicate then drops under the already-set setPreserveUnreferencedObjects(false). Keep the byte-identical signature detection (FNV hash + the five dict keys), the objGen != guard, and the per-pair try/catch.
- New staged fixture: distinct_duplicate_streams.pdf in $TMPDIR - two distinct indirect stream objects with byte-identical raw data and matching signatures. tasks.title: Dedup signature includes /SMask, /Mask, /Type, /Intent so masked streams never merge (ESC-015)
tasks.description: Extend the byte-identical dedup signature in PDFOptimizer's dedup loop (currently /Subtype /Width /Height /ColorSpace /BitsPerComponent /Filter /DecodeParms + raw-byte hash) to also key on /SMask, /Mask, /Type and /Intent, so two byte-identical image streams that differ only by carrying a soft/color-key mask are never merged (which would repoint referrers and silently change transparency). Add a regression fixture/test proving the masked pair stays distinct while matching pairs still dedup.
acceptance_criteria: Given two byte-identical indirect image streams that match on every existing signature key (/Subtype /Width /Height /ColorSpace /BitsPerComponent /Filter /DecodeParms) but differ in that one carries an /SMask (or /Mask), when optimized with defaults (deduplicateStreams=true), then the two streams are NOT deduplicated - no referrer is repointed, both stream objects remain, and result.streamsDeduplicated does not count the masked pair - so transparency is not silently changed.

Given the dedup signature key set, when a byte-identical stream pair differs on /SMask, /Mask, /Type or /Intent, then that difference is part of the signature and prevents the merge, while a byte-identical pair that also matches on these keys (e.g. neither carries /SMask) still deduplicates with streamsDeduplicated>=1.

Given the existing dedup tests, when the signature fix lands, then the P2-T6 distinct_duplicate_streams test (streamsDeduplicated>=1 with defaults, ==0 with --no-dedup) and the P1-T3 shared-XObject checks still pass.
